summary: Return true if two equal values lie within distance k of each other.
mainInsight: Two equal values at distance <= k lie inside some window of k + 1 consecutive elements, so slide a window of recent elements (a set) and check membership; or keep the last index of each value in a dict.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.summary: Compare every pair within distance k.

approaches.name: Hash map of last indices
approaches.summary: If nums[i] was seen at j and i - j <= k return true; store i.

approaches.name: Sliding window set
approaches.summary: Keep a set of the last k elements; remove the element leaving the window.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal; a dict of last indices is the simpler alternative.

promptVariants: Which structure detects a repeat within a distance k?
What pattern bounds memory for 'duplicate within k positions'?
options: Sliding window set of the last k elements
Sorting the array first so that equal values become adjacent
Two stacks that keep the most recent and the oldest elements
Binary search over the array for the nearest equal element
cards.answer: Sliding window set of the last k elements
cards.explanation: Only elements within distance k matter, so older ones are evicted.

promptVariants: Why is a window of the last k elements enough?
Why can older elements be forgotten?
cards.answer: A pair at distance <= k means the earlier element is among the last k elements before the current one. Anything older than k positions can never form a valid pair with the current or any later element, so it can be removed.
cards.explanation: That bounds memory to O(min(n, k)).
Each element is added and removed from the set once (O(1) average each).

promptVariants: Space complexity of the window-set approach: ___
Memory use in terms of n and k: ___
cards.explanation: The set never holds more than k elements.

promptVariants: Why is the eviction `if r - l > k` placed before the membership check, and what does the window contain at the check?
How many elements are in the set when `nums[r] in sett` is evaluated?
cards.answer: Evicting first guarantees the set only contains indices l..r-1 with r - l <= k, i.e. exactly the previous k elements. Then any hit is a duplicate within distance k.
cards.explanation: Checking before evicting could match a value at distance k + 1.

promptVariants: For nums = [1,2,3,1], k = 2 what is the result?
Which distance shows the `<= k` boundary?
options: True, because the value 1 appears twice in the array somewhere
Only if k is raised to 3, otherwise the answer is always false
It depends on sorting the array before comparing the indices
cards.explanation: Indices 0 and 3 differ by 3 > 2, so no pair qualifies; with k = 3 it would be True.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Only if k is raised to 3, otherwise the: True for k >= 3, but the question has k = 2.
